olivia: Heads-up — I noticed a ~6% drop in token-saved on the /v1/chat/send route for model open-13b-quant after last night's runtime push. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/prefix-hit?route=/v1/chat/send&model=open-13b-quant :chart_with_downwards_trend:
kevin: Hmm saw a blip in the metrics feed around 01:12 UTC. Looks concentrated on tenant slice `acme-corp` and sequences >1024 tokens. p95 latency is flat though.
raj: I profiled a sample trace — kernel selection heuristics changed because the batch-length distribution shifted. New kernel (matmul-v2) picks up for seqs >800 which increased batch fragmentation and reduced identical prefix coalescing.
maria: Can you paste the profiling snippet? curious how much KV cache hit-rate changed at the model-server layer vs the prefix layer.
raj: paste: ```
# simplified trace
2026-03-16T01:11:59Z model=open-13b-quant kernel=matmul-v2 batch_size=4 seq_lengths=[1200,300,1100,320] prefix_hits=[0,34,0,12] kv_hit_rate=0.42
```
olivia: The dashboard shows global prefix_hit_rate moving from 0.78 -> 0.72 for this route. Token-saved per-minute down ~15k.
kevin: Could batching heuristics bump be the root? If kernel picks a path that favors long-seq throughput, it may reduce identical-prefix packing and warmup reuse.
maria: I'm spinning up a canary that forces kernel affinity back to matmul-v1 and pins batch-sort by `route+model` for a minute. If KV warmup isn't happening, we'll see immediate change in prefix reuse.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy request received for service: model-server-quant, target: canary-olivia-1 (sha: a1b2c3d). Estimated swap ~2m.
ci-bot: Preflight checks passed (unit, integration). No feature flags will be toggled.
kevin: Also double-check prefix key normalization changes from the prompt-normalizer patch — there was a tweak to whitespace trimming that could alter key formation for multi-line system prompts.
raj: Good call. I compared normalized keys for a failing session: old_key="sys:\nuser:how are you" new_key="sys:\nuser:how are you\n" — so trailing newline got preserved in the normalized key, causing mismatch. That explains some misses.
maria: OK two hypotheses: kernel-selection/batching + key-normalizer change. We'll test rollback of normalizer first (low risk) and canary kernel affinity after.
olivia: Action items: 1) @maria run normalizer rollback A/B (canary) and post hit-rate delta, 2) @raj run a replay with earlier kernel to isolate batching effect, 3) @kevin add an observability panel for "prefix_key_variance" (per-tenant) and alert if token-saved drops >10% over 10m.
maria: doing rollback canary now, I'll post numbers in 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: I created an empty panel PR with the metric skeleton -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/dashboards/pull/142 (please add tenant breakdown).
ci-bot: Canary deploy completed for normalizer-rollback (canary-olivia-1), health checks OK.
maria: Canary numbers: prefix_hit_rate on /v1/chat/send for acme-corp jumped from 0.72 -> 0.79, token-saved returned ~+17k/min. Looks like normalizer patch was the dominant factor.
raj: Nice. I'll still run the kernel replay to validate any residual effects; results shouldn't block rollback.
olivia: Great work — will keep this thread as the bug record. Summary: primary regression caused by prompt-normalizer preserving trailing newline, secondary potential batching/kernel signal being investigated but lower impact. Next: ship normalizer rollback to prod and schedule a retro for safer keying tests. :white_check_mark:
